name: Game On!

pick.hint: Or click one to choose it.
pick.label: Pick something dull
pick.heading: Pick something dull and turn it into a video game
lead: People will happily spend 200 hours in a game farming pretend vegetables, driving a pretend lorry across Europe or running a pretend hospital. Ask them to do the real thing for ten minutes and they suddenly have a headache.
Choose a boring job, chore or everyday task and turn it into a game nobody can put down. Here are some ideas, but you can choose your own. Some of these games *already exist*. Yours will be better.
pick.note: I don’t need a business plan or a single line of code. Some ideas will sound like a hit and some will sound like a punishment. Both are welcome.

rows: Which boring task are you turning into a game?
What’s the goal? Points, levels, a final boss, a high score?
Rewards, rankings, a story, other players, the fear of losing your streak…
Who plays it first? People who do it for real, people who never would, someone else?
What makes it more than just doing the chore on a screen?
Which streamer, event or place gets everyone talking?

values.goal: Wardrobe Wars: build a wardrobe before your flatmate gets home. You win if it stands up, the doors close and there are no screws left over. There are always screws left over.
values.hook: A world leaderboard for every product. Somewhere in Sweden, someone has built a bookcase in four minutes, and you won’t rest until you’ve beaten them.
values.who: Anyone who has ever moved flat in Berlin, which is everyone, and couples who want to know whether they’ll really last.
values.twist: It’s two-player, and each of you only gets half of the instructions, so you have to talk to each other. That’s the final boss.
values.promote: A live tournament in a big furniture store in Lichtenberg, streamed on Twitch, with a free hot dog for every finished bookcase.

yours.label: Your game
yours.heading: Your idea
yours.lead: Fill it in on your own phone or laptop (it stays on your device), and be ready to tell the class about your game in a few sentences.

rank.label: The ranking
rank.heading: Which game wins?
rank.lead: Each student tells us about their game in a few sentences. Add it, then argue it into place until everybody agrees.
